decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up left-arm approach toward the horizontal mallet handle, raising clearance and gradually turning the gripper downward.
Continue a smooth, open-gripper approach over the handle; maintain elbow-up continuity.
Align the downward gripper with the left portion of the mallet shaft, approaching above the grasp height.
Use wrist view to center the shaft between the fingers; make a shallow downward and lateral correction before closing.
Close the left gripper on the visually centered mallet shaft, holding position for a stable pickup.
Lift the closed gripper and verify visually that the mallet rises before orienting it over the first key.
Mallet is visibly retained. Raise additional clearance and rotate the shaft toward the xylophone while staying in the left workspace.
Add vertical clearance before completing the turn toward the first red key; tip height remains visually uncertain.
Correct the rejected tensor; approach the first red key from the unchanged pose, with the right arm stationary.
Lower vertically for the first red-key strike; retain the mallet and inspect contact before the required lift.
Lift more than 0.025 m after the red-key contact, then move right above the orange key while keeping the left-hand grip closed.
Strike the second, orange key vertically, then lift the mallet 0.05 m before moving to the next key.
Translate above the third yellow key at lifted height, then make its vertical strike.
Lift the mallet clear of the yellow key by 0.05 m, then align above the fourth green key.
Strike the fourth green key, then lift 0.05 m before repositioning for the blue keys.
Keep the left wrist in its own workspace while turning the raised mallet tip rightward over the fifth cyan key.
Strike the fifth cyan key and lift the retained mallet by 0.05 m, leaving the wrist left of center.
Reorient the lifted mallet over the sixth dark-blue key, compensating forward as the shaft turns right; keep the left wrist in its workspace.
Make the sixth dark-blue-key strike, then lift 0.05 m while keeping the mallet closed in the left gripper.
Turn the lifted tip toward the seventh violet key, moving forward to preserve its strike line while keeping the left wrist left of center.
Strike the seventh violet key with a small centering correction, then lift the mallet 0.05 m before the final key.
Align the lifted mallet above the eighth magenta key, retaining orientation and keeping the left wrist on the left side of center.
Replan from the interrupted pose: lower with small increments to relieve the joint limit, and turn the mallet slightly right to center the final magenta key.
Finish the eighth magenta-key strike, pause briefly at contact, then lift the mallet by 0.05 m while keeping it held.
Raise the mallet well clear after the final strike, retreating left and back to preserve elbow-up joint margin and verify visible tip lift.
Keep the mallet visibly clear of all keys after the left-to-right sequence, settling in a safer left-workspace holding pose.
Hold the retained mallet safely above the keys after the final lift; avoid extra contacts while the episode remains active.
Contact registration is unconfirmed. Return above the first key with ample clearance for a deliberate left-to-right pass with clear contact dwells and lifts.
Reapproach the red key, compensating left for the current held-mallet angle while descending slowly toward contact.
Center the tip on the red key, dwell briefly at the strike depth, and lift 0.06 m before proceeding rightward.
Move at lifted height to the orange key, descend for its strike, and pause so the tip-contact geometry can be checked before lifting.
Lift the mallet 0.06 m after orange contact, then align above the yellow key without touching intervening surfaces.
Lower onto the yellow key with a small rightward centering correction; inspect the visible tip before lifting.
Lift 0.06 m from yellow, then translate above the fourth green key while maintaining the closed left-hand grasp.
Strike the green key, dwell briefly, and use a larger 0.10 m lift to ensure visible mallet-tip clearance despite possible shaft pivoting.
Reorient the raised mallet toward the fifth cyan key, compensating forward without crossing the left wrist into the right workspace.
Center and strike the cyan key, dwell at contact, then begin a vertical lift before proceeding to dark blue.
Complete a high lift after cyan contact, then rotate and advance the retained mallet above the sixth dark-blue key.
Strike the sixth dark-blue key with a short contact dwell, then begin a 0.05 m lift while retaining the mallet.
Increase tip clearance after dark blue, then turn and advance over the seventh violet key without crossing the left wrist past center.
Strike the seventh violet key with a short contact dwell and lift 0.05 m before the final key; preserve elbow-up continuity.
Add clearance after violet and align the held tip with the eighth magenta key, staying left of center and slightly back for joint margin.
Strike the final magenta key vertically, dwell briefly at contact, then lift the held mallet 0.05 m.
